title: Zuriel Chapter Introductions — Proverbs 1–31
description: Chapter-by-chapter study guides for all 31 chapters of Proverbs, with wisdom context, reflection questions and KJV-checked key passages.

chapters.title: Proverbs 1 — Wisdom's call and the two ways
chapters.historicalContext: Proverbs is a collection of wisdom instruction, sayings and poems associated in its headings with Solomon and other named sages. Chapter 1: The opening instruction introduces wisdom as teachable reverence for God and warns against joining violent schemes. Wisdom is personified as calling publicly at the crossroads. The collection brings together teaching from different settings; do not assume every saying was written at the same time or in one original speech.
chapters.overview: The chapter contrasts the invitation of wisdom with the lure of violence, greed and refusal to listen.
chapters.studyObservation: Notice the images, contrasts, repeated themes and practical concerns in Proverbs 1. The chapter contrasts the invitation of wisdom with the lure of violence, greed and refusal to listen. Read individual sayings in their literary and social context.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read Proverbs 1 alongside the book's opening call to wisdom and its repeated concern for the fear of the Lord. The opening instruction introduces wisdom as teachable reverence for God and warns against joining violent schemes. Wisdom is personified as calling publicly at the crossroads. Compare related sayings without forcing every proverb into an identical rule.
studyQuestions: What contrast, instruction or image is central to Proverbs 1?
How does the chapter connect wisdom with speech, relationships, work, justice or worship?
How can its guidance be applied faithfully without treating a proverb as an unconditional promise?
chapters.lifeApplication: Practise the wisdom of Proverbs 1 through honest choices, careful speech and concern for others. The chapter contrasts the invitation of wisdom with the lure of violence, greed and refusal to listen.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: Proverbs usually offers general wisdom observations rather than guarantees that every life will follow the same outcome. The opening instruction introduces wisdom as teachable reverence for God and warns against joining violent schemes. Wisdom is personified as calling publicly at the crossroads. Do not weaponize its counsel to shame victims or excuse injustice.
chapters.readingNote: Read Proverbs 1 as part of Israel's wisdom literature. Consider the saying, poem or instruction form, its audience and its moral purpose; distinguish general patterns from absolute promises.
